481   // Each of the 5 clock gateable domains (periph, safety island, security island, spatz and pulp
482   // cluster) have the following clock distribution scheme:
483   // 1. For each domain the user selects one of 3 different clock sources (host clock, alt clock and
484   //    per clock). Each of these main clocks are either supplied externally, by a dedicated PLL per
485   //    clock source or by a single PLL that supplies all three clock sources. The configuration of
486   //    the clock source is handled by the external PLL wrapper configuration registers.
487   // 2. The selected clock source for the domain is fed into a default-bypassed arbitrary integer
488   //    clock divider with 50% duty cycle. This allows to use different integer clock divisions for
489   //    every target domain to use different clock frequencies.
490   // 3. The internal clock gate of the clock divider is used to provide clock gating for the domain.
491 
492 for (genvar i = 0; i < NumDomains; i++) begin : gen_domain_clock_mux
493   clk_mux_glitch_free #(
494     .NUM_INPUTS(3)
495   ) i_clk_mux (
496     .clks_i       ( {periph_clk_i, alt_clk_i, host_clk_i} ),
497     .test_clk_i   ( 1'b0                                  ),
498     .test_en_i    ( 1'b0                                  ),
499     .async_rstn_i ( host_pwr_on_rst_n                     ),
500     .async_sel_i  ( domain_clk_sel[i]                     ),
501     .clk_o        ( domain_clk[i]                         )
502   );
503 
504   // The register file does not support back pressure directly. I.e the hardware side cannot tell
505   // the regfile that a reg value cannot be written at the moment. This is a problem since the clk
506   // divider input of the clk_int_div module will stall the transaction until it is safe to change
507   // the clock division factor. The stream_deposit module converts between these two protocols
508   // (write-pulse only protocol <-> ready-valid protocol). See the documentation in the header of
509   // the module for more details.
510   lossy_valid_to_stream #(
511     .T(domain_clk_div_value_t)
512   ) i_decouple (
513     .clk_i   ( host_clk_i                        ), // Connected to host clock since the soc_ctr
514                                                     // regs are clocked with it
515     .rst_ni  ( host_pwr_on_rst_n                 ), // See above
516     .valid_i ( domain_clk_div_changed[i]         ),
517     .data_i  ( domain_clk_div_value[i]           ),
518     .valid_o ( domain_clk_div_decoupled_valid[i] ),
519     .ready_i ( domain_clk_div_decoupled_ready[i] ),
520     .data_o  ( domain_clk_div_value_decoupled[i] )
521   );
522 
523   // We have to synchronize the division value into the clock domain of the undivided source clock.
524   cdc_4phase #(
525     .T(domain_clk_div_value_t)
526   ) i_cdc (
527     .src_rst_ni  ( host_pwr_on_rst_n                 ),
528     .src_clk_i   ( host_clk_i                        ),
529     .src_data_i  ( domain_clk_div_value_decoupled[i] ),
530     .src_valid_i ( domain_clk_div_decoupled_valid[i] ),
531     .src_ready_o ( domain_clk_div_decoupled_ready[i] ),
532     .dst_rst_ni  ( pwr_on_rsts_n[i]                  ), // Use POR-only on both sides. Partial reset
533                                                         // problem for SW-reset is thus not
534                                                         // possible.
535     .dst_clk_i   ( domain_clk[i]                     ),
536     .dst_data_o  ( domain_clk_div_value_synced[i]    ),
537     .dst_valid_o ( domain_clk_div_valid_synced[i]    ),
538     .dst_ready_i ( domain_clk_div_ready_synced[i]    )
539   );

542     .DIV_VALUE_WIDTH(DomainClkDivValueWidth),
543     .DEFAULT_DIV_VALUE(1),
544     .ENABLE_CLOCK_IN_RESET(1)
545   ) i_clk_div (

547     .rst_ni         ( pwr_on_rsts_n[i]               ), // Only reset during power-on. Software
